## 431. Precedence and its links; what can be born next against what continues (UE13)

UE, a unified explanation of reality, asks in its sixth item to state the root's laws on causal sets and to ask what continuation relative to a class adds to an order, and in its seventh whether widening the adjacent possible can give 生生 its second-order direction ([plan](../../development/ue-unified-explanation/PLAN.md)). UE10 read the possible on any process ([§424](424.md#424-what-a-course-keeps-reachable-ue10)) and UE11 the possible relative to what is held ([§429](429.md#429-where-the-possible-grows-ue11)). UE13 reads causal set theory and its classical sequential growth on the root and on processes, and compares what can be born next with what continues ([note](../../development/ue13-causal-sets/NOTE.md)).

**Its standing.** Every law is near-definitional, a witness or a calibration. That a locally finite order is the transitive closure of its covering relation is known, as is that it can fail where an interval is infinite; that stems reverse the inclusion of precedence is the order-reversing correspondence between orders on one set and their down-sets, the specialization order of an Alexandrov topology, with Birkhoff's representation of finite distributive lattices a neighbour; internal temporality and the timid and gregarious children are Rideout and Sorkin's (2000). The calibrations, excluded middle for reaching every pair by links and for finding the pair a widening loses, are lemmas of the laws that need them: telling a direct condition from a longer chain, and which pair a widening loses, are found by deciding. The witnesses of the courses' start say which comparisons need it. What is new is reading these against the theory's direction: the reversal on the growth's courses, the two readings it reverses and the extremes, renewal on the configurations and their limits, the finer-class witnesses and the kinds of birth up to relabelling.

**A count, not a law.** Counted by brute force over every causal set of one to five elements ([script and output](../../development/ue13-causal-sets/count)), the kinds of next birth, the births up to relabelling, are fewest for the antichain and the chain, `n + 1` each, tied with others, and most for configurations mixing precedence and unrelated elements: at three elements the two-chain with a point has six kinds and every other causal set four; at four the most is nine, a single pair with two points; at five sixteen, a configuration with three pairs and no symmetry. The enumeration finds 1, 2, 5, 16 and 63 causal sets up to relabelling, the known counts of finite orders. Not proved in Lean: an upper bound on kinds needs the stems decided. The re-check reran the count byte for byte and recounted it by an independent method.

**The review and the fix round.** The [review](../../development/ue13-causal-sets/REVIEW-UE13.md), with 46 Lean probe theorems, found every proof of the first draft correct with an empty axiom report, the reading of Rideout and Sorkin's growth faithful and the core law correctly scoped, and the prose saying more than the Lean in several places: the reach of links was claimed both ways where only one inclusion was proved, decidability was called the constructive form of finiteness, `ω + 1` was read as showing that the links reading needs discreteness, the stems were called the converse of precedence without their exact forms, the starts of courses were left out, and the reading of the adjacent possible ranked by what C is not read on. All 22 findings were taken (the note's §7): the probes' laws moved into the module, the module grew from 56 to 107 theorems, law 1 became a record of its own homed at 01 §1, and the readings were rewritten to say what C is read on and which 生生 is meant. The relabelling law (the note's law 8) was added after the review.

**The re-check.** The [re-check](../../development/ue13-causal-sets/RECHECK-UE13.md), with 60 Lean probe theorems, found the Lean sound, the relabelling law right in substance, the count right and the split into two records right, and fourteen findings, six of them for before landing. The two calibrations were excluded middle, not the De Morgan law the module had proved them to imply. The courses' start was left out of fourteen docstrings and of the note, and most of those laws are false without it. The reading left calling widening better a choice that the continuation condition's scope had already made, since every widening of what can be born next loses continuation, a loss the condition counts. The argument for which 生生 is meant inferred D1 from the grammar's 生生 failing, though it holds on the chain's limit. A slogan and a contest name had returned. All fourteen were taken (the note's §8): the probes' laws moved into the module, which grew to 161 theorems in 212 declarations, with the witnesses of the start in a namespace of their own, and the readings were rewritten.

**Decisions at landing.** One module, two records: law 1 is a claim about the root's precedence, distinct from the growth, so it is homed at 01 §1, and the rest at 07 §2; each declaration is cited by one record, and the growth record depends on the precedence record for `Causet`, the links and the three-element witness. The logic review's question L-02 (4), whether precedence as the reach of a condition relation is a sound basis for an order of time compared with causal sets, is answered in part, with the decision kept; the review packet is re-synced by its owner, not edited here. In the Chinese texts the links are 覆盖 (covering), since 链 names the chain. The witnesses live in namespaces of their own (`OmegaPlusOne`, `Undecided`, `Halves`, `Finer`, `Kinds`, `Starts`), and `Becoming.CausalGrowth` clashes with no name of the package. The calibrations are stated as excluded middle together with what the need says about the unfolding, and the order that never reverses widening is named by what it does (`not_above_antichain`), not by a contest.

**Readings** [AI reading, D45]. Causal set theory leaves open which course of its growth is better; what the growth bears on, for the theory's direction, is what calling widening better (C) is read on, a first-order matter. Read on what can be born next, widening loses precedence and ranks highest the course in which nothing conditions anything, where nothing continues; read on what continues, it ranks highest the chain. The continuation condition counts every continuation's losses, and every widening of what can be born next loses continuation, so with the scope it fixes the reading is on both together; there two courses differing by a pair are mixed, and ordering them needs a measure, a premise beyond C and the condition. The second order is not reached: every course keeps widening what can be born next. In the grammar 生生 names only renewal without end, which holds on no configuration and, of the extremes' limits, only on the chain's; the 生生 meant is generation generating generation (01 §6), which asks more than renewal of lines, and it is not the order read on what can be born next, since the widest course transmits no condition; that it is not the order read on what continues needs a further premise, that admitting at each offset the fewest ways to go on also falls short. Kauffman's tentative law, that a biosphere may, on average, enter its adjacent possible as fast as it can sustain, read on the pasts has its widest course lose all precedence; read on kinds of birth the extremes are incomparable at offset 2, and the count finds them with the fewest kinds for opposite reasons and configurations with many pasts and few symmetries with the most; counting is scale, which the second-order direction does not count.
